requirements.statement: Ledger balance validation must compare exact per-currency sums, not modular Int64 sums; in the database a commerce ledger transaction is created as draft, posts only with entries that sum to zero in every currency, keeps its entries unchanged once posted, never returns to draft, and is reversed only by a posted transaction.
requirements.authority: approved AUTHORITY-069
requirements.property: per-currency accumulated sum uses arbitrary precision
requirements.verification: Integer type and inspected conversion before accumulation; 512 actual-module boundary sequences and Hspec regressions for the helper. Runtime SQL posting check exercised on the production schema (balanced, unbalanced, cross-currency, [M,M,2] wrap, extreme balanced, empty) with a disabled-trigger negative control. Bounded TLC model of ledger posting with five negative controls and the ledger-posting-postgresql spec against the fully migrated schema (formal/system/ledger-posting.md). Legacy-upgrade fixtures and witnessed two-session reversal races under READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ run in scripts/__tests__/ledger-posting-upgrade.py. The canonical provider retry/refund harness applies both the ledger integrity and fixed-line snapshot migrations before its store integration cases; its reduced domain fixture does not establish every production-domain guard (docs/payments/consolidation-2026-10-15.md). Snapshot schedules in ledger-posting-snapshot.py test entry INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE before posting (blocked and already committed), post-first and writer rollback, across READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE. Six lock-only mutation controls reproduce posted balance 1; these finite PostgreSQL tests do not discharge complete implementation/refinement obligations. Non-owner TEMP and caller-schema shadowing checks plus two lookup-removal controls exercise the installed guards; the finite LedgerNamespace model abstracts these lookup choices (formal/system/ledger-namespace.md). The startup schema verifier rejects missing, reordered or caller-controlled lookup settings, missing expected function signatures and SECURITY DEFINER drift for both installed ledger guards. Transaction-scoped full-schema mutations and a compatible extra-GUC case run through the actual rendered verifier; migration receipts remain unchanged. Changes to the installed schema verifier, ledger/provider/expiry runners and ledger regression harnesses must select backend=true, so the full-schema PostgreSQL controls are executed rather than silently skipped. The path-classifier regression checks nine affected paths against the real selector.

A poster at READ COMMITTED validates the committed entries; an older REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE poster fails with SQLSTATE 40001. Post-first mutation attempts reject or serialize-fail. Database: SQLSTATE 23514 for creation in any status but draft, posting without entries or unbalanced in any currency, entries inserted/updated/deleted after posting, posted -> draft, draft -> reversed, reversal by a non-posted transaction, and any change of a reversed transaction. A referenced posted reverser cannot itself be reversed. Migration rejects existing empty/unbalanced posted rows and self, draft or reversed reversal targets before installing new guards. Stale snapshot posting or entry mutation may return SQLSTATE 40001; callers must roll back the whole transaction. The additive write-fence migration separately refuses empty or unbalanced posted/reversed history.
requirements.recovery: Preserve existing evidence. Migration fails before replacing guards if posted history is empty or unbalanced or a reversed transaction lacks a distinct posted reverser. Reconcile the invalid history through an explicitly reviewed repair before retrying; the migration never silently changes ledger amounts or references.

No writer uses 'reversed' today; the reversal rule bounds a future writer.
validateLedgerBalance (Haskell) has no runtime caller; the database rule is the enforced one.

Before 2026-10-12 the database validated balance only on draft -> posted, so a transaction inserted as posted or an entry appended after posting was not rejected; the ledger posting integrity migration closes both.

The #551 lock-only entry guard admitted stale-snapshot unbalanced postings under REPEATABLE READ. The additive 2026-10-16 write fence repairs the reproduced schedules; unbounded SQL/MVCC refinement, caller retry policy and deployed correspondence remain open.

Unqualified trigger lookup admitted non-owner TEMP shadowing on source 59df1dd2a17952b906cf89d1c5502725d51239e1. The additive namespace migration pins both functions; runtime trusted-schema privileges, owner/DDL bypass and deployed correspondence remain unverified.

Startup verification checks the installed trusted lookup settings and invoker boundary, not arbitrary trigger bodies or privileged DDL equivalence; a table owner can still disable or replace triggers.

requirements.title: Consolidate authoritative ticket admission, inventory and transfer boundaries
requirements.statement: Ticket admission must consume a paid issued unused event-scoped ticket at most once with its audit in the same transaction; inventory holds must respect tier/event capacity; accepted transfer must rotate the credential and revoke former-holder projection. Checkout quantity must not exceed the approved versioned per-order limit; approved/retired commercial policies cannot regress to draft or lose immutable history. Approved tax-inclusive pricing must preserve advertised integer totals for every accepted quantity, conserve total = organizer payable + platform fees + tax, and retain the purchased mode immutably; an event-specific tax rate is independently authorized. An unresolved signed-provider refund or reversal bound to the same checkout/capture/merchant must fence admission even when legacy rows still say paid and issued. PayPal capture requires an authenticated readback of the original provider order, with unchanged internal-order, merchant, amount and currency validation before marking paid. Zero platform fees must create no zero-valued ledger entry while cash, organizer payable, tax and nonzero fees conserve the captured total. A verified external refund/reversal received before capture binding leaves durable merchant-scoped evidence after inbox retry exhaustion; later binding must fence admission without a webhook replay. Canonical orders reject legacy bulk status mutations. Refund routing follows the unique succeeded provider, retaining existing non-PayPal request behavior. Retained issued tickets of partially refunded orders remain transferable under the purchased policy. OAuth failure before a refund POST leaves the request retryable; ambiguous POST outcomes retain the no-repeat fence. Accepted provider refund identities survive mismatched monetary responses so exact authenticated readback can reconcile without another POST. Whole-ticket partial refunds accept any eligible subset matching the stable cent allocation. An authorized guest order receipt remains accessible when public ticket sales close; receipt lookup failure must not offer a replacement purchase.

requirements.title: Fresh database readiness without private failure detail
requirements.statement: A ready HTTP response requires a successful fresh SELECT 1 through the application database pool. A probe discards pooled connections PostgreSQL has closed, retrying up to the pool size plus one inside its deadline, so one request answers ready once the database is back. Pool or query failure of every attempt and expiry of the two-second cooperative deadline return 503 with fixed non-private fields; every readiness response forbids caching.

requirements.concurrency: Each request includes pool acquisition in its deadline; runtime cancellation must propagate. System.Timeout is cooperative and cannot bound uninterruptible native operations or prove release writer exclusion. The attempt budget is the pool size of TDF.DB.makePool plus one (source-bound check): a pool cannot hold more stale connections than its size, and one attempt must remain for a live connection.
requirements.idempotency: Read-only independent observations; retry cannot reuse a cached positive observation.
requirements.failure: Synchronous exception on every attempt (at most the pool size plus one), negative probe or expired deadline yields 503. Runtime cancellation propagates through every attempt.

requirements.observability: Exact handler HTTP checks, source-bound verifier output and deployed read-only probes; record source and time.

requirements.verification: Actual Haskell boundary tests and six detected controlled mutations; real HTTP handler tests with failed pool and SQLite query. No formal runtime refinement proof. Real PostgreSQL HTTP harness disables connections only to its nonce-owned database, terminates its sessions, requires fixed503 repeatedly, reenables connections and requires recovery. Attempt retry: Haskell probe tests (stale-then-live, budget exhaustion, final negative result, cancellation through retry) (the mutations include single attempt, no retry and cancellation swallowed in the retry; the attempt budget is bound to the pool size plus one); the PostgreSQL harness first leaves more idle pooled connections than it makes degraded probes, so the probes must discard the terminated connections within their own attempts (with one attempt per probe the recovery probe took the next terminated connection and failed, 2026-10-12). ReadinessProbe.tla: ProbeReportsDatabase over every stale count and database state for PoolSize 4; the one-attempt and pool-size budgets fail it (the model found that a budget of the pool size is one short).

requirements.statement: A public consent request must not activate WhatsApp consent. It records a pending request; claiming a confirmation request is one conditional update allowed only when the number has no request in the last 24 hours, and simultaneous first requests for a number do not fail. A request the provider did not accept stays pending as undelivered: for 1 hour from the request the number can still confirm it by messaging first and a new public request may retry the send without changing the request instant; afterwards it waits for the 24-hour interval. Delivered requests to a number are therefore at least 23 hours apart. Consent becomes active only through one conditional update when the same number sends an affirmative keyword whose Meta message timestamp is no earlier than the pending request, within 7 days of a delivered request, and the request has not been withdrawn since; a concurrent withdrawal wins and a delayed or replayed earlier reply cannot confirm a newer request. The confirmation request uses the approved template named by WHATSAPP_CONSENT_TEMPLATE when configured; the person may also message SI first (VITE_WHATSAPP_OPTIN_URL). Public responses never disclose a number's consent state; the public consent lookup returns 410 without reading consent data. Opt-out (public form, inbound STOP/SALIR/BAJA/CANCELAR or staff revocation) always withdraws consent and invalidates any pending request without resetting the 24-hour interval, and its stored instant is never earlier than the request it defeats; neither withdrawing, confirming nor staff capture lets anyone request another message early. The public opt-out notifies only a number that was subscribed. The failure of a superseded send attempt changes nothing. Staff consent capture remains admin-only.

requirements.title: Canonical music releases with immutable approved versions
requirements.statement: Music releases are authored as versions owned by a verified artist or authorized team. Each version moves only through music_valid_transition; approval freezes an immutable snapshot and SHA-256; correcting a published release creates a related version that references the same immutable asset bytes. Publication and withdrawal are applied by locked database functions that handle each due candidate on its own: a candidate that fails at publication is suspended with its error and the other candidates still publish; publishing a version retires every other formerly published version of its release that is still published, replacement_pending or takedown_scheduled, and reopens a withdrawn release; a failure that is transient (deadlock, serialization failure, lock timeout) leaves the candidate scheduled for the next run; the release points at the version it last published only while that version is published, suspended, replacement_pending or takedown_scheduled. Only a published, in-embargo-window, territory-allowed version is public.

requirements.title: Quarantined uploads, reproducible processing and signed asset access
requirements.statement: Audio and artwork uploads go by scoped SigV4 multipart to a quarantine bucket under a UUID key. The worker re-downloads, recomputes SHA-256, inspects the real type, produces reproducible derivatives (AAC/FLAC/preview/artwork) with a versioned manifest, and only then promotes the original bytes as immutable. Public asset URLs are signed for five minutes only after music_public_asset_accessible re-resolves version, embargo, territory and policy; masters are never publicly signed.

asset uploaded -> inspecting -> valid (master, immutable, master bucket) with derivatives inserted ready and immutable
job queued/retry -> running (claim, attempt+1) -> succeeded | retry (run_after delayed) | dead_letter at or beyond max_attempts (an expired last attempt is reclaimed once more)
running -> reclaimed by another run only after the lease expired

Public signature for a master asset

A completion written by a run whose job was reclaimed (attempt token mismatch)
Reclaiming a job whose lease is still live

requirements.concurrency: Worker claims one due job FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; every later statement of the run is prefixed by the lease guard (version row FOR NO KEY UPDATE, job row FOR UPDATE, status running, same worker name, same attempt, lease younger than the ttl); multipart completion is idempotent per upload; derivatives are unique per (version, role, sha256).
requirements.idempotency: Re-running a job reproduces identical derivatives for identical input. A re-upload with the same declared SHA-256 binds to the existing non-promoted asset row and re-points it at the new object before inspection (trg_music_rebind_upload_asset); the asset's queued, retry, running and dead-lettered attempts are cancelled (a cancelled run is stopped by the lease guard).
requirements.failure: Type, size or checksum mismatch fails the attempt without promotion; the job retries with a growing delay until max_attempts, then dead_letter, and the version becomes validation_failed. A lost or expired lease stops the run (lease-lost marker, USR1) and the job is reclaimed.
requirements.recovery: Failed jobs are retried with a growing delay; an expired lease lets another run reclaim the job. Orphan multipart uploads created by the worker's own PUTs are aborted per worker-multipart.md; client upload sessions have no purge (ambiguity). After a checksum-mismatch dead letter, uploading the correct bytes under the same declared hash is inspected and the earlier attempts, running ones included, are cancelled (2026-10-12_music_upload_rebind).
requirements.observability: Worker logs and job status rows; worker-regression-diagnostics.md.
requirements.verification: S3 spec, local HTTPS S3 probes, Linux worker image smoke and integration against local PostgreSQL/S3; bounded TLC model of leased processing with three negative controls and an over-limit reclaim witness (formal/system/music-asset-processing.md)

requirements.title: Private reproducible DDEX ERN 4.3.2 export of approved versions
requirements.statement: A DDEX ERN 4.3.2 message is a projection of one approved version snapshot hash. The API commits export and job atomically, serializes per actor/key and version, revalidates queued exports against the same rules used by API, renderer and worker, and produces a private, reproducible package with message-bound file names. No delivery to partners is performed.
requirements.authority: Unreviewed recovered local implementation; docs/music-releases/ddex-*.md; AUTHORITY-082 (state sets, lifecycle guards and failure-report privacy recorded)
requirements.source: Local main work of 2026-09-11..2026-09-16 recovered onto main in PR #510; docs/music-releases/ddex-operation-lifecycle.md
requirements.property: Every exported package is reproducible from, and bound to, exactly one approved snapshot hash.
preconditions: music_releases.ddex_export enabled
Version approved with immutable snapshot

state.authority: music_ddex_export.status and music_processing_job.status; transitions are enforced by the worker's conditional UPDATEs under the lease guard, not by a trigger

allowedTransitions: API: request -> export queued + generate_ddex job queued in one transaction (actor/key advisory lock, version row lock)
Worker gate 1 (rules re-checked under the lease guard): queued | validation_failed | generating -> generating
Worker gate 2 (rules re-checked, same snapshot hash): generating -> valid with xml/manifest/package assets, then job succeeded
Any failure of an attempt: not-valid export -> validation_failed and job retry; on the last attempt -> failed and job dead_letter, in one write
A valid export whose job did not close is recovered as is: job succeeded, nothing regenerated
Authorized replay of the original request: a queued export without a job gets its job; otherwise the existing export is returned unchanged
forbiddenTransitions: Export of a non-approved version
Export job committed without its export row
valid -> any other status; a valid package is never regenerated or re-pointed
failed -> any other status; no replay re-enqueues a failed export
A write by a process whose claimed attempt is no longer the job's attempt
Partner delivery
effects: Private package with credits, parties and identifiers of that version
requirements.authorization: Creating an export requires strict administrator access (and the music_releases.ddex_export flag); listing and downloading require release.downloads on the release or strict administrator access, re-checked by the backend.
requirements.privacy: Packages are private and contain collaborator identifiers; never public.
requirements.concurrency: API: pg_advisory_xact_lock(music-ddex:<actor>:<key>) then the version row FOR UPDATE; export and job commit together. Worker: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim; every later statement runs under pg_temp.music_worker_guard (version FOR NO KEY UPDATE, job FOR UPDATE, status running, same worker name, claimed attempt as fencing token, lease younger than the ttl); a running job is reclaimed only after its lease expired. Gate 1 and gate 2 lock both registry rows FOR SHARE in UUID order and share their transaction with the status write. Bounded model: MusicDdexExport.tla.
requirements.idempotency: Replaying the request with the same actor, key, version, operation, sender and recipient returns the existing export; a different body under the same key is 409; the natural key (version, recipient, operation, snapshot) is unique, so a second request for the same package is 409 whatever its key. The replay recreates only a missing job of a queued export and never resets attempts.
requirements.failure: A gate refusal stores the field-level report (valid=false, code ddex_preconditions_failed, errors[]). Any other failure of an attempt (renderer, transfer, checksum, crash handler) stores a fixed message with its error code; the worker's stderr summary is kept on the job row until the next claim clears it, and permanently once dead-lettered. The export becomes validation_failed while attempts remain and failed with the dead letter; a valid or failed export is never changed by a later attempt.
requirements.recovery: Queued revalidation and replay per ddex-queued-validation.md and ddex-atomic-enqueue.md; a valid export is recovered without regeneration after a crash between gate 2 and job closure. A failed (dead-lettered) export has no recovery path: see ambiguity.
requirements.observability: Export status and validation report (release downloaders); job status, attempts, error code and stderr summary (operators).
requirements.verification: ERN spec against fixture and schema, package builder tests, enqueue fault-injection probe. Bounded TLA+ model of the export/job lifecycle under two leased processes with five single-guard negative controls (formal/system/music-ddex-export.md). Worker runtime test (PostgreSQL, substitute renderer/packager/transport): commit gate, revocation during rendering, valid recovery, queued revalidation, and the processing-failure report that excludes worker stderr and recovers to valid on retry.
requirements.evidence: Local results in docs/music-releases/ddex-atomic-enqueue.md (2026-09-16); TLC 1.7.2 and the worker runtime test on PostgreSQL 16, 2026-10-13 (formal/system/music-ddex-export.md).
requirements.confidence: Medium for schema conformance; partner acceptance unknown.
ambiguity: Partner-specific profiles and delivery are out of scope; compatibility matrix is a 2026-09-12 snapshot.

A dead-lettered export (status failed) has no recovery path: the natural unique key (version, recipient, operation, snapshot) rejects a new request for the same package and the replay never re-enqueues a failed export, so a transient outage lasting the five attempts (about 15 minutes) blocks that operation for that version and recipient until an operator edits the rows. The same holds for any non-queued export whose job was cancelled by hand. ADR-018 chose no blind retry; an audited operator retry is an open product decision.
The job's stderr summary is served to the uploader through the upload status endpoint (MusicReleaseUpload.hs); that surface belongs to MEDIA-MUSIC-ASSET-001 and is not changed here.
The export's validation_failed status is also used for processing failures that are not validation refusals; the report's code distinguishes them.

conformance.reason: Lifecycle, fencing, finality and failure-report privacy are modelled within bounds and exercised by the worker runtime test locally; the export feature flag is off in production, and dead-letter recovery is undecided.

requirements.title: Music downloads only through verified purchase entitlements
requirements.statement: A music purchase order references one rule, release version and price in integer minor units and opens a commerce checkout session in the music_download domain. Only server-verified provider evidence bound to the order marks it paid; the projection settles a payable purchase and grants exactly one entitlement, ending it on refund or chargeback. Verified money for a closed purchase follows PAY-MUSIC-OUTCOME-001 and grants no entitlement. Entitled and free downloads use the same downloadable-asset predicate, count each new request identifier against the entitlement limit, answer a repeated identifier only while its signed URL is valid, and issue URLs that live 300 seconds. A free grant that was revoked is not revived by a new request.

requirements.source: Local main work of 2026-09-11..2026-09-16 recovered onto main in PR #510; docs/music-releases/architecture-and-data-model.md

paid -> refunded -> entitlement revoked

Download of master or unavailable asset

A signed URL for a request identifier whose first URL has expired
revoked or expired free grant -> active by request
effects: One entitlement per paid order
Audited, limited download URLs

requirements.privacy: Purchase and download audit is visible only to the buyer and authorized staff.
requirements.concurrency: One order per buyer and idempotency key by unique constraint; entitlement creation is trigger-enforced and unique per order; download authorization holds the entitlement row lock while it counts and inserts.
requirements.idempotency: Repeated order creation and repeated recording of the same verified payment change nothing; a repeated download request identifier is answered without counting for 300 seconds and refused afterwards.
requirements.failure: Unverified payment leaves no entitlement. Payment-attempt failure does not cancel the purchase. Verified money received for a closed purchase is retained for reconciliation without reopening fulfillment under PAY-MUSIC-OUTCOME-001. Ambiguous provider transport and recovery remain open.
requirements.recovery: Refund revokes entitlement; no royalties, subscriptions or settlement.
requirements.observability: Download audit rows and checkout session events.
requirements.verification: Bounded TLA+ model with six negative controls; PostgreSQL tests of the purchase handler, verified-payment record, triggers, download authorization and flag gate, with reversion checks of the three repairs; read-only SQL contract of the shared predicate. Provider calls are not exercised.
requirements.evidence: Local TLC, PostgreSQL 16 and Hspec on 2026-10-10.
requirements.confidence: Medium for the payment record, entitlement and download rules, which run on PostgreSQL in tests; low for the provider calls and failure handling, which are untested and have open defects.
ambiguity: No live payment provider wiring for music_download has been verified.
Music payments bypass the shared payment runtime and the production provider switches; only the commerce flag for the checkout environment gates them.
A failure after the provider charged leaves no reconciliation record; no webhook or reconciliation path exists for this domain.
Partial refunds keep the entitlement and disputes revoke it permanently; both need a product decision.
Download limits count authorizations, not transferred bytes; a replay retains the original 300-second expiry. Cross-provider admission and ambiguous transport recovery are not established.

conformance.reason: Payment record, entitlement and download rules are modeled within bounds and exercised on PostgreSQL; provider calls are untested and several failure-path defects are open. Commerce is disabled by default and should stay disabled until they are closed.

requirements.title: Single persistent web player and public music pages
requirements.statement: One PlayerProvider owns a single HTMLAudioElement mounted above all navigation. The queue persists asset ids and renews short-lived authorization on select or retry; position and preferences are bounded; Media Session, keyboard, focus and accessible messages are centralized. Public catalog, library and release pages render only what the public API returns. The legacy radio widget is hidden on /musica routes; playback analytics use a stable identity with retry-safe ingestion.

requirements.title: Personal single-use artist invitation links grant the Artist role by automatic policy
requirements.statement: An admin issues a personal invitation link for one named artist. The link carries a random token whose SHA-256 digest alone is stored; it expires after 30 days by default (at most 90) and can be revoked while unused. A signed-in user who opens the link redeems it: the backend atomically binds the link to the first redeeming account and applies the artist.invitation.artist automatic assignment policy (trigger artist-invitation-redeemed) to grant only the non-administrative Artist role, records the onboarding intent and returns a refreshed session. Public campaign names are never accepted as invitations.

requirements.title: Approved artist onboarding access requests provision the Artist role
requirements.statement: An access request for feature artist.onboarding with action create is the only feature/action pair with a code-owned grant role (Artist). Since the 2026-09-16 self-service decision, creating that request activates the requester's own Artist profile through the artist.self-service.artist policy and records the request as approved by system-policy; the reviewed path remains only for requests created before that decision. Any reviewed decision requires a reviewer distinct from the requester, Admin for grant-bearing pairs, a request that is still pending and not past its expiry; approval publishes a sensitive-publication security revision with the requester as author and reviewer as approver and applies the grant atomically. All other approvals remain manual. The web page explains which outcome applies and shows the review link only to users allowed to review.
requirements.authority: Unreviewed recovered local implementation
requirements.property: A role is provisioned from an access request only for artist.onboarding/create, and only by one of two paths: (a) self-service, where createRequest activates the requester's own artist profile and records the request approved by system-policy with no reviewer; a non-administrator receives Artist through the artist.self-service.artist policy, while an administrator receives no Artist role so the strict Admin scope is preserved; (b) a reviewed decision on a request that is still pending and not past expiry, made by an administrator distinct from the requester, with a published revision. No path grants an administrative or emergency role. Automatic paths never reactivate a revoked assignment; a reviewed approval may restore one as an explicit, published and audited administrator decision.

requirements.statement: Course registration and ticket checkouts that require acceptance show the approved policy's terms and cancellation/refund text before the acceptance control, send the accepted terms version, and the server rejects a missing (tickets) or stale (courses and tickets) version for the policy it is about to bind.

Policy changed after display -> 409 -> new terms shown and acceptance cleared

Clients send the accepted version; mismatch returns 409 with a review-again message

requirements.privacy: Terms text is public policy content; no personal data added.
requirements.concurrency: Policy is re-read at checkout; a concurrent policy change surfaces as 409 rather than binding stale terms. Terms-identity migration locks both policy tables before preflight and retains the locks through atomic trigger installation; concurrent writers cannot introduce conflicting history in that interval.
requirements.idempotency: Accepted version is validated before the existing idempotent hold logic; replays with the same version behave as before.
requirements.failure: Missing ticket acceptance returns 400; stale version returns 409; clients reload the policy and clear acceptance.

Database test of the terms-version identity triggers (scripts/test-checkout-policy-terms-identity-migration.sh). Scope-only course/event reassignment is checked against destination terms; matching and unused destination versions remain permitted. Independent guard-removal controls reproduce conflicting reassignments for each table. A controlled PostgreSQL barrier witnesses a conflicting writer after preflight and before trigger DDL for each table; the original migration admits both texts, while the fenced migration blocks and then rejects the writer. TermsIdentityUpgrade checks the finite two-scope upgrade boundary with three expected counterexamples; this does not prove whole checkout consent, arbitrary schedules or SQL refinement. Historical policy snapshots also fence version reuse after deleting the last live policy or editing it in place. Full-schema SQL checks cover course and event history, identical replay and a distinct new version. Independent old-guard controls admit the forbidden reuse; conflicting historical preflight controls fail closed. The finite history model covers two scopes, one version and two texts, not all production schedules. Both retained policy-history tables also reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE while continuing to append legitimate snapshots. Six independent full-schema regressions expose the missing guards; six selective guard-removal controls require the named rejection and exact guard restoration. The finite model retains independent disclosed text so archive erasure cannot erase the invariant, with separate delete/update/truncate counterexamples.
requirements.evidence: Exact-revision CI receipt required before claiming conformance.

conformance.reason: Display and binding are implemented and unit-tested; a database-backed runtime receipt is still required.

Report an empty refresh as successful while retaining old chunks.
Commit public-index deletion if replacement insertion fails.
Skip legacy cleanup because the index is fresh or an embedding provider/configuration is unavailable.
Raw rejected stored URLs or route-unreachable course identities -> embedding payload.
Disclose a captured production identity shared by multiple Text-normalized stored course rows.
effects: The next admitted worker check or administrator refresh removes legacy non-course chunks locally without a provider call; public replacement remains a separate transaction.
Source entities are not deleted; external provider records and backups are not erased by reindexing.
requirements.authorization: Existing administrator and worker admission remains unchanged. Index source selection is enforced in the backend, independently of retrieval guards.
requirements.privacy: Explicit product decision on 2026-10-13: public courses only; stop indexing private material. This policy concerns index refreshes, not a claim that query embeddings or other assistant provider payloads are public.
requirements.concurrency: One refresh captures public documents from statement snapshots before embedding and atomically replaces the index. Parallel refresh ordering/freshness is not guaranteed; all revised writers still construct only course chunks. Retrieval separately checks current course metadata. Cleanup and replacement are separate transactions. Deployment must drain old mixed-source writers; no claim covers privileged external SQL writers or rollback to the old builder. Each constructed document reads its fields, earliest session and collision inputs in one SELECT snapshot.
requirements.idempotency: Repeated successful refreshes replace the derived index; provider requests may repeat and chunk identifiers/timestamps are not stable.
requirements.failure: Cleanup SQL failure aborts before embedding. Model/schema mismatch and provider/count errors return Left after legacy cleanup; replacement SQL errors propagate after rollback of public replacement. A missing index table skips cleanup and fails existing schema validation.
requirements.recovery: Retry failed public refreshes while retaining existing public chunks. Do not restore non-course chunks or roll back to a mixed-source builder. Historical backups and provider-held data require separate retention/erasure decisions.
requirements.observability: PostgreSQL tests capture adapter payloads and persisted rows, check empty-corpus no-call behavior, provider/count refusal and SQL rollback. Existing administrator result and index statistics report refresh outcome. Aggregate source counts verify cleanup without disclosing content; tests cover a fresh index and invalid configuration before provider admission.

requirements.title: Fresh payment intents use database time after checkout locking
requirements.statement: A fresh canonical payment intent may be admitted only if the locked checkout expires strictly after database wall time sampled after acquiring its row lock. Caller audit timestamps and transaction/statement start time do not authorize admission. A live, otherwise eligible checkout is not refused solely because its audit timestamp is in the future.
requirements.authority: Existing createPaymentIntent expiry rejection; PAY-RETRY-001 closed-checkout denial; explicit financial correctness and concurrency mandate.
requirements.property: At the admission sample, admitted implies databaseTime < lockedExpiry; refused-for-expiry implies databaseTime >= lockedExpiry.
preconditions: Canonical checkout and economic binding exist; ordinary PostgreSQL row locks remain enabled.
Database wall clock and timestamp ordering are authoritative for expiry; privilege/DDL bypass is excluded.
inputs: Database wall time after row lock
allowedTransitions: Waiting -> locked -> sample database clock -> admitted only before expiry.
Exact authorized runtime attempt replay remains on its separate existing read-only path.
forbiddenTransitions: Stale request time admits a fresh intent after expiry.
Transaction-start time or a clock sampled before the row-lock wait admits an expired checkout.
Equality with expiry admits a fresh intent.
effects: Rejected expiry inserts no intent or amount component.
Accepted creation retains the supplied audit timestamp without using it as admission authority.
requirements.authorization: Current caller/session, economic binding and provider qualification remain independent preconditions; no authorization control is relaxed.
requirements.privacy: Synthetic owned database and fixed test identities; no real payment provider or customer data.
requirements.concurrency: First lock the checkout row; then sample clock_timestamp() in a separate database statement. Test actual pg_blocking_pids witnesses at READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ.
requirements.idempotency: No change to existing attempt/intent key binding or authenticated replay semantics.
requirements.failure: Expiry rejection returns Left and creates no intent/components; SQL errors remain caller-owned rollback failures.
requirements.recovery: A refused fresh intent requires current valid checkout authority; already-contacted operations require their existing reconciliation/replay flow.
requirements.observability: Retain exact source hashes, Git revision, tool versions, observed lock waits, named mutation failures and TLC counterexamples.
requirements.verification: Seven actual-store PostgreSQL examples; three independently compiled clock mutants must reach assertion failures; finite TLC model and four named negative configurations. Existing backend-quality and event-operations-formal CI lanes enforce execution.
requirements.evidence: formal/system/evidence/2026-10-25-payment-intent-expiry/receipt.json; replay commands and limits in formal/system/payment-intent-expiry.md. Evidence is valid only for its recorded source hashes.
requirements.confidence: TESTED store boundary and BOUNDED_VERIFIED finite abstraction; whole implementation equivalence is UNKNOWN.
ambiguity: Admission is the post-lock time sample, not transaction commit or provider HTTP completion.
Clock rollback, arbitrary schedules, whole-program refinement and finality of external money remain unverified.
This does not retrofit every legacy payment writer or activate providers.

conformance.reason: Scoped implementation tests and finite model controls; hosted candidate CI and independent review remain required. No whole-program refinement or provider-completion proof.

requirements.title: Posted ledger identity, source and audit headers are immutable
requirements.statement: An UPDATE whose existing commerce ledger transaction is posted or reversed must preserve every column value except status and reversal_of. Draft edits and value-preserving writes remain permitted; lifecycle transitions retain their independent existing validators.
requirements.authority: Explicit user mandate for immutable posted accounting records; accepted ADR-0104 immutable financial events and compensating corrections.
requirements.property: OLD.status in {posted,reversed} and accepted UPDATE implies projection(NEW)=projection(OLD), where projection removes only status and reversal_of.
preconditions: Registered posting, entry write-fence and namespace guards remain enabled; the lifecycle cannot reopen a draft.
The actor cannot modify trusted DDL, replace functions, bypass triggers or change replication mode.

state.header: All columns other than status and reversal_of

allowedTransitions: Draft header edit.
Identical posted/reversed header update, including the entry parent-write fence.
Independently validated posted-to-reversed lifecycle transition.
forbiddenTransitions: Changing a posted/reversed primary key, source identity or audit column.
Committing a draft-era source edit after a concurrent posting has committed.
effects: Invalid header updates reject atomically; no financial history is rewritten.
requirements.authorization: This integrity guard grants no caller, refund or payout authority. Ordinary non-owner fixtures have header SELECT/UPDATE, no entry UPDATE and no trusted-schema CREATE.
requirements.privacy: Only synthetic owned disposable PostgreSQL fixtures; no customer or provider data.
requirements.concurrency: A stale header writer must preserve the row after an observed posting lock wait. Named RC/RR/SERIALIZABLE schedules use pg_blocking_pids; PostgreSQL may serialize-fail a repeatable snapshot.
requirements.idempotency: Preserve the original source-key anchor; this does not establish exactly-once provider charges or all caller replay behavior.
requirements.failure: SQLSTATE 23514 for a differing posted header, or SQLSTATE 40001 for a conflicting repeatable snapshot; failed operations do not alter committed source attribution.
requirements.recovery: Authorized compensating transactions; keep the additive guard through application rollback. Historical attribution repair and deployment retain separate approval.
requirements.observability: Record exact Git/source hashes, tool versions, actual blocking witnesses and named negative controls.
requirements.verification: Full registered schema ordinary-role SQL updates, rollback-scoped guard/startup mutations, witnessed posting/header races under three isolations, a guard-removal RC counterexample and a finite two-writer TLC model with a named mutation control. Backend and formal CI lanes enforce execution.
requirements.evidence: formal/system/evidence/2026-10-26-ledger-header-main/ records current-main composition; formal/system/evidence/2026-10-25-ledger-header/ retains earlier source identities. Replay commands and limits: formal/system/ledger-header.md. Admit evidence only for its recorded relevant source hashes. Saved-search historical-prefix compatibility is tracked separately in formal/system/evidence/2026-10-26-saved-search-checkpoint/; original financial/model receipts retain their source identities.
requirements.confidence: TESTED named SQL boundary and BOUNDED_VERIFIED finite abstraction; complete implementation equivalence remains UNKNOWN.
ambiguity: No proof of arbitrary installed function bodies, whole-program refinement, all interleavings, liveness, owner/superuser resistance or deployed correspondence.
Status/reversal semantics and correction authority remain separate obligations.

conformance.reason: Scoped SQL tests and finite model checking do not discharge complete implementation/refinement obligations; independent review and production approval remain required.
